whatItDoes: Simulates paying off a credit card balance with a fixed monthly payment. It applies the card's monthly interest and shows the payoff time, total interest, and total paid.
whyItExists: A card balance grows because monthly interest can outpace the minimum payment. Seeing exactly how many months a fixed payment will take — and how much interest accumulates — helps people choose a realistic payment that actually reduces the balance.
whoShouldUse: Anyone carrying a credit card balance who wants to know how long it takes to clear at their current payment, or how much faster extra payments finish the job.
useCases: See how long the balance takes at the current payment
Compare payments to find an affordable acceleration
Understand how much interest the balance will cost
Set a payoff milestone for a specific card
instructions: Read the payoff months, total interest, and total paid
bestPractices: Pay more than the monthly interest so the balance actually falls
Stop adding new purchases while paying down
Consider balance-transfer offers with care about fees
Round the payment up to shave both months and interest
commonMistakes: Paying only the minimum — the payoff can stretch for decades
Using a payment at or below the monthly interest (never finishes)
Ignoring that new purchases add to the balance
Assuming the APR applies once a year instead of monthly
faq: Is this financial advice? — No, it is a planning estimate.
What if my payment only covers the interest? — The balance never decreases and the payoff plan cannot finish.
Does it include new purchases? — No, it assumes the balance is fixed.
Are my numbers shared? — No, the simulation runs locally in your browser.
